Let’s reason through this.  

The “maximum sustainable power” refers to the highest power output an athlete can maintain for the duration of an event without fatiguing prematurely.  

- (A) “usually remains constant during a race” — This is false because fatigue causes power output to drop over time in most endurance events.  
- (B) “declines with the distance of the race” — This is plausible: longer races require a lower average power to be sustained, so the maximum sustainable power is lower for longer distances.  
- (C) “is improved by a high fat diet” — Not necessarily true; high-fat diets can increase fat oxidation, but maximal sustainable power depends more on aerobic capacity and glycogen availability, not fat intake alone.  
- (D) “is inversely related to muscle glycogen content” — False; higher muscle glycogen generally supports higher sustained power in endurance events.  

The most accurate is (B) — as race distance increases, the maximum power an athlete can sustain for the whole race decreases.  

Final answer: (B)
